question: Is Lumen DB 4.2 faster than 4.1?
claim: Lumen DB 4.2 reduced median query latency by 30% compared with version 4.1 on the TPC-H benchmark.
note: Two independent, reliable sources state the figure.

evidence.title: Lumen DB 4.2 release notes
evidence.text: Release notes for Lumen DB 4.2. The new vectorized join operator is enabled by default. On the TPC-H benchmark at scale factor 100, median query latency fell by 30% compared with Lumen DB 4.1. Write performance is unchanged.

evidence.title: Reproducing analytical database benchmarks
evidence.text: We independently reproduced the vendor's TPC-H results. At scale factor 100, Lumen DB 4.2 showed a 29-31% reduction in median query latency relative to version 4.1 across five runs on identical hardware.

question: What are the Kestrel API rate limits?
claim: The Kestrel API limits free-tier accounts to 60 requests per minute.
note: Stated directly in official documentation.

evidence.title: Kestrel API rate limits
evidence.text: Rate limits. Free-tier accounts may send up to 60 requests per minute. Paid plans start at 600 requests per minute. Requests above the limit receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

question: Is Orbis Robotics cutting jobs?
claim: Orbis Robotics laid off about 12% of its staff in March 2026.
note: One news report, directly stated.

evidence.title: Orbis Robotics to cut 12% of jobs
evidence.text: Orbis Robotics, which makes warehouse robots, said on Tuesday it would cut roughly 12% of its workforce, about 140 jobs, as it refocuses on warehouse automation. The layoffs were announced in March 2026 and take effect immediately.

question: How many workers should the Pebble web server run?
claim: Running the Pebble web server with twice as many workers as CPU cores improves throughput for I/O-bound workloads.
note: Two low-reliability but independent first-hand reports agree.

evidence.title: Tuning Pebble workers
evidence.text: In my tests, running Pebble with workers set to two times the number of CPU cores gave the best throughput for our I/O-heavy API. Going higher than that added context-switching overhead and throughput dropped again.

evidence.title: Pebble worker count?
evidence.text: We doubled Pebble workers relative to cores on our I/O-bound service and saw throughput go up by about 40%. CPU-bound endpoints did not benefit.

question: Do heat pumps work in cold climates?
claim: Air-source heat pumps in the Northfield program kept a coefficient of performance above 2.0 at -15 °C.
note: Government field study plus independent news coverage of it.

evidence.title: Northfield heat pump field monitoring
evidence.text: Field monitoring of 85 air-source heat pumps in the Northfield program found that the units maintained a coefficient of performance above 2.0 even at outdoor temperatures of -15 °C. Household energy costs were not part of the monitoring program.

evidence.title: Heat pumps beat expectations in Northfield
evidence.text: A government study in Northfield reported that the heat pumps it monitored stayed above a COP of 2 at minus 15 degrees Celsius, outperforming what installers had predicted.

question: Is the Gizmo 3 router reliable?
claim: The Gizmo 3 router overheats when its firmware is updated over Wi-Fi.
note: A single forum anecdote states it.

evidence.title: Gizmo 3 overheating during update
evidence.text: Happened to me twice: updating the Gizmo 3 firmware over Wi-Fi made the router overheat and reboot halfway through. Over Ethernet the update was fine.

question: How long does Tidewater keep queued messages?
claim: Tidewater's managed queue service retains messages for up to 14 days.
note: The vendor's own blog announces it.

evidence.title: Longer message retention
evidence.text: Today we are extending message retention in Tidewater Queues from 7 to 14 days for all customers, at no extra cost. Messages older than 14 days are deleted automatically.

question: Do workplace wellness programs reduce sick days?
claim: In the 2016 Harlow trial, the intervention group reported 18% fewer sick days than the control group.
note: A peer-reviewed trial states it, but it is ten years old.

evidence.title: A randomized trial of a workplace wellness program
evidence.text: In a randomized trial of 640 office workers in Harlow, participants in the intervention group reported 18% fewer sick days than those in the control group over 12 months (95% CI 11-25%). Effects on productivity were not measured.

question: Does the Marlow vaccine candidate work?

note: Hedged, early, small, not peer reviewed.

evidence.title: Early data on the Marlow vaccine candidate
evidence.text: Early results from a small phase 1 study suggest the Marlow candidate may reduce infections by as much as 90%. Researchers cautioned that the figure comes from just 40 participants and has not yet been peer reviewed.

question: Does -O3 make Quill programs faster?
claim: Compiling with the Quill compiler's -O3 flag makes programs 25% faster.
note: Holds only for numerical code; the claim drops that condition.

evidence.title: Quill optimization benchmarks
evidence.text: On our numerical benchmark suite, -O3 builds of Quill programs ran 25% faster than -O2 builds. On I/O-bound programs we saw no measurable difference.

evidence.title: Trying Quill -O3
evidence.text: Switching my matrix code to -O3 in Quill gave me roughly a 25% speedup. I have not tried it on anything else yet.

evidence.title: Brackenridge county solar costs, 2015

evidence.title: Kestrel API rate limits

evidence.title: Kestrel trims its entry plan

question: Do remote teams ship faster?
claim: Remote teams at Corvid Labs shipped features faster than co-located teams.
note: Two sources support it; one first-hand account disputes it.

evidence.title: Remote work and delivery speed: evidence from 48 teams
evidence.text: Across 48 teams at Corvid Labs, remote teams completed features 12% faster than co-located teams on median cycle time over one year.

evidence.title: Corvid Labs data favours remote teams
evidence.text: Corvid Labs' internal data, as described in a recent study, showed its remote teams shipping features faster than teams sharing an office.

evidence.title: What the Corvid numbers miss
evidence.text: As a Corvid Labs engineer, I think the study got it backwards: once code-review delays are counted, our co-located teams actually shipped features sooner than the remote ones.

question: Does Zephyr tea lower blood pressure?
claim: Drinking Zephyr tea lowers blood pressure.
note: An anecdote supports it; a controlled government study finds no effect.

evidence.title: Zephyr tea and blood pressure
evidence.text: My blood pressure dropped noticeably after a month of drinking Zephyr tea every morning.

evidence.title: Zephyr tea controlled study
evidence.text: A placebo-controlled study of 210 adults found no significant change in blood pressure among participants who drank Zephyr tea daily for eight weeks.

question: Which web server uses less memory, Pebble or Corso?
claim: The Pebble web server uses less memory than the Corso web server.

evidence.title: Pebble's memory footprint
evidence.text: In our benchmark, Pebble used 40% less memory than Corso under the same load of 10,000 concurrent connections.

evidence.title: Corso memory facts
evidence.text: Our measurements show that Corso's memory footprint is lower than Pebble's at every concurrency level we tested, from 100 to 10,000 connections.
